title: Localization of the ideal multiplication kernel
statement: Let $R,S,R',S'$ be commutative rings with compatible algebra maps $R\to S$, $R\to R'$, $S\to S'$ and $R'\to S'$ giving the same map $R\to S'$. Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, let $M$ be an $S$-module with restricted $R$-action, and put $J=IR'$, $N=R'\otimes_R M$, $M'=S'\otimes_S M$. Suppose there are a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq S\otimes_R R'$ and a ring map $q:S\otimes_R R'\to S'$ with $q(s\otimes r')=\sigma(s)\varphi'(r')$, making $S'$ the localization at $W$. Let $\mu_N:J\otimes_{R'}N\to N$ and $\mu':J\otimes_{R'}M'\to M'$ be multiplication, and $c_N,c'$ the respective tensor symmetries. There exists an $R'$-linear map $\alpha:N\otimes_{R'}J\to M'\otimes_{R'}J$ satisfying $\alpha((r'\otimes x)\otimes b)=(\varphi'(r')\cdot(1\otimes x))\otimes b$ for all $r'\in R',x\in M,b\in J$, and for every $z\in\ker\mu'$ the element $c'(z)$ lies in the $S'$-linear span of $\{\alpha(c_N(y)):y\in\ker\mu_N\}$. There is no quotient-flatness hypothesis. The displayed formula determines $\alpha$ uniquely by two tensor inductions.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00MO, second proof paragraph, with Tags 00CS and 00DK

proof.text: Use tensor cancellation to identify the base-changed module with the localization of the ordinary base-change module and apply exactness of localization to the multiplication kernel.

Construct alpha by tensoring the canonical localization map with the identity of J and conjugating by tensor symmetry. A localized kernel element is a fraction of an ordinary kernel element y by localization exactness. Its image is q(w) inverse times alpha(c_N(y)), so it belongs to the S-prime span of those images. This uses no ordinary base-change kernel-generation theorem.
